You don't have a remote configured yet. Let me check your git config and help you set up authentication for when you do add a remote.

For git push without password prompts, here are the best options on Windows:

**Option 1: SSH Key (Recommended)**
Most secure approach for internal remotes:

```powershell
# Check if you have an SSH key
Test-Path ~/.ssh/id_rsa

# If not, generate one (press Enter for defaults when prompted)
ssh-keygen -t rsa -b 4096 -f $env:USERPROFILE\.ssh\id_rsa

# Start SSH agent and add your key
Get-Service ssh-agent | Start-Service
ssh-add $env:USERPROFILE\.ssh\id_rsa
```

Then add your remote using SSH format:
```powershell
git remote add origin ssh://git@internal-server/path/to/repo.git
```

**Option 2: Git Credential Manager (Easier for HTTPS)**
Windows has Git Credential Manager built in for HTTPS URLs:

```powershell
git config --global credential.helper wincred
```

When you push, it'll prompt once, then store the credential securely.
